change_and_reason: Baseline: grayscale, global Otsu, keep every connected component. Eggs are bright, so a single global threshold is the simplest possible detector.
Keep only the largest component, since most images contain one egg; tests whether fragment false positives dominate the error.
Lab L channel instead of gray: perceptual lightness, less affected by colour casts.
Whiteness map L - 1.5*chroma: eggs are bright AND colourless, so penalising chroma should suppress bright coloured backgrounds (pink bowls, green leaves, skin).
Add morphology (open 7, close 7) + hole filling to remove speckle and fill specular/shadow holes inside eggs.
Add shape filter on components (area, solidity, IoU with fitted ellipse, axis ratio): eggs are convex ellipses, background blobs are not.

Replace single Otsu with a 12-level threshold sweep (40th-97th percentile) and pick the most egg-shaped components across levels (greedy NMS by ellipse score). One global threshold cannot fit egg-on-white and egg-on-dark scenes alike.
T07 + reject candidates not at least 15 grey-levels brighter than a 21px ring around them: many T07 false positives were flat elliptical background patches.
T07 but rank candidates by shape score x min(1, contrast/40) so bright-against-background ellipses win the NMS over flat ones.
T07 + keep only candidates scoring >= 0.85 x the best one in the image (most images have 1-3 similar eggs; weaker extra candidates were mostly false positives).
T07 + area bonus 0.3*sqrt(area) in the ranking: nested sweep candidates (highlight inside egg) are both elliptical; prefer the larger whole egg.
Combine the two kept Stage-B changes (T09 contrast-aware score + T10 relative keep).

T12 + marker-controlled watershed refinement (fg = candidate eroded 0.5r, bg = outside candidate dilated 0.5r, flooded on the blurred colour image). Dev error maps showed the threshold keeps only the lit side of the egg; the shaded side is lost (low recall).
T13 + area bonus (T11) so the whole egg rather than its highlight seeds the refinement.
T12 + GrabCut (GMM colour model + graph cut, 3 iters, init from candidate) instead of watershed, as an alternative boundary refinement.

T13 + extra candidates from closed Canny contours (auto thresholds, dilate 3, fill holes). On white paper/boxes the egg has the same whiteness as the background, but its outline is still a visible edge.
T13 with background-normalised whiteness (subtract 0.5 x Gaussian-blurred map, sigma 60): eggs on bright backgrounds and ash-covered eggs are locally brighter even if globally not.
T13 with stricter ellipse-fit threshold 0.8 -> 0.85: several wrong picks were roughly elliptical paper/cloth regions.
T13 with stronger chroma penalty 1.5 -> 3.0 to push coloured backgrounds (skin, pink bowls, leaves) further down.
T13 with a wider/denser sweep (20th-97th percentile, 16 levels) so darker / ash-covered eggs get a threshold level too.
Combine T17 (local whiteness) + T18 (ellipse IoU >= 0.85).
T21 + Canny closed-contour candidates (T16 gave +0.004 alone).
T21 with stronger background subtraction (local_w 0.5 -> 0.8).
T21 with a smaller background scale (sigma 60 -> 30 px), closer to egg size (r ~ 40-120 px).
T21 with a larger background scale (sigma 60 -> 120 px).
T22 but ellipse threshold back to 0.80 (T21 showed 0.85 adds nothing once local whiteness is used; looser may recover eggs with flattened outlines).
T22 with looser relative keep 0.85 -> 0.7 to recover second/third eggs in multi-egg images (instance recall is the weak point).
T22 with a wider watershed band (inner 0.35r, outer 0.7r): lets the refinement reach further into the shaded side of large eggs.
T28 + looser ellipse threshold 0.8 (T26 was marginally better than T22 with it).
T28 but replace each instance by its fitted ellipse before refinement: eggs are near-ellipses, so this should regularise ragged threshold outlines.
T28 + distance-transform watershed split of components that fail the shape test (touching eggs merge into one non-elliptical blob).
T28 with an even wider refinement band (inner 0.25r, outer 0.9r).
